findings.id: 3.8-missed-1 (review-notes item 9: B&B assumes monotone costs, objectiveScore unchecked, negative scalar costs accepted)
findings.rootCause: Branch-and-bound pruning and winner selection add scalar objectives and assume each one is a finite, non-negative cost. PackedCostSession.objectiveScore is a provider hook (LmdbFrontierStatisticsCostSession and test providers override it), and its result was never checked. A negative objective made a plan look cheaper than free. A negative or NaN objective also reached PackedCandidateArena.append, which throws IllegalArgumentException('invalid packed candidate row'), so a single bad provider value failed the whole planning run.
findings.change: EventSourcingPackedCostSession is the provider boundary: every production planning run wraps its session in it (PackedCascadesPlanner:480-481), and replay uses it too. It now routes both objectiveScore() and the five trace.append objective arguments through a new private providerObjective(). That method passes finite, non-negative values through unchanged and maps negative, NaN or infinite values to Double.MAX_VALUE, the packed planner's existing saturated or unknown cost. This matches PackedIncumbentSearch.objectiveIncrement and the saturatedAdd helpers. Because every objective entering the planner is now non-negative, cost sums stay monotone. That also settles the critique minor about PJE's saturatedAdd not rejecting negative sums while PIS's does: the two now behave the same. PackedCostAlgebra's NaN-propagating comparisons are unreachable, because PackedCostVectorArena:97-99 rejects NaN and negative components at write time.

findings.rootCause: Planner deadlines are absolute System.nanoTime() values, and the JDK allows that clock to have any origin, so readings and deadlines can be negative. Two canonical constructors, OptimizationGoal and PackedPlannerLimits, mapped deadlineNanos <= 0 to Long.MAX_VALUE, silently turning a legal deadline into 'no deadline'. OptimizationGoal.asBudgeted also computed its overflow check as Long.MAX_VALUE - now < nanos. For a negative now, that subtraction overflows, so the budgeted deadline became unbounded.
findings.change: Long.MAX_VALUE is now the only 'no deadline' sentinel. The <= 0 mapping is removed from both canonical constructors, and both records document the contract. asBudgeted delegates to a new package-private OptimizationGoal.deadlineAfter(now, timeout), which saturates only on real overflow (now > MAX - timeout). No caller in core or tests passed 0 or a negative value to mean 'no deadline'; every no-deadline caller already passes Long.MAX_VALUE. LmdbCascadesOptimizer.withExplicitConfiguredDeadline already used the correct overflow form. PackedSearchBudget still compares with nanoTime() >= deadline, which is right because deadlines saturate instead of wrapping. The subtraction form would wrongly treat a far-past deadline as unexpired.

findings.id: 3.8.2-residual (found in the bR diff review: the tie-break digest hashed parser-generated anonymous variable names)
findings.rootCause: The b1 canonical tie-break digest (PackedRelationDigest) hashed every node's getSignature(), including Var names. The SPARQL parser names anonymous variables (blank nodes, collections, path intermediates) with a counter in query-text order (BlankNodeVarProcessor:76-84: _anon_bnode_N). So a textual permutation of blank-node patterns renames them, changes the digests, and flips the plan chosen among exactly tied alternatives. Four equal-estimate blank-node star patterns across 24 orders gave 16 different plans.
findings.change: PackedRelationDigest.meet(Var) hashes a fixed ANONYMOUS_VARIABLE token for an anonymous Var without a value, and delegates to meetNode otherwise. Constants, which are anonymous Vars with values, and named variables keep their full signature, so predicates and constants still discriminate. A digest collision only falls back to the existing state-id tie-break.

findings.rootCause: LmdbFactorCostAssembler maps overflow and non-finite totals to Double.MAX_VALUE, so LMDB can inject saturated costs into the packed cost stream.
findings.change: No code change, deliberately. Double.MAX_VALUE is the packed planner's own saturation value (PJE/PIS saturatedAdd, objectiveIncrement, and now providerObjective). It is finite, so PackedWinnerTable accepts it, and since b1 ties among saturated costs are broken by the canonical content digest, not by text order. Remapping only LMDB to a smaller ceiling (such as CostVector's 1e15 UNKNOWN_COMPONENT_ROWS) would rank a genuinely overflowed plan below a real 1e16-row plan, which is critique 3.8.1 point (b). Any finite double ceiling at or above ~1e16 loses additivity, exactly as MAX_VALUE does. The real fix is roadmap 4.4's log-space, confidence-quantile objective.
findings.deferredReason: Needs roadmap 4.4, a log-space objective shared by PackedJoinEnumerator, PackedIncumbentSearch, PackedCostAlgebra and LmdbFactorCostAssembler. That redesigns the objective scale and is outside this reconcile batch.

findings.id: critique reconciliation 3.8.1 (major: finite ceilings; minors: PackedCostAlgebra NaN, dead UNKNOWN_ROWS_CEILING, CostVector.INFINITE)
findings.rootCause: See the b1 finding 3.8.1: CostVector mapped unknown components to MAX_VALUE, and EstimateVector.filter treated a pass ratio as a row count.
findings.change: Every item is handled in the tree. Major: the packed 1e60/1e150 ceilings were not adopted (b1 deviation). joinRows and saturatedAdd still saturate at MAX_VALUE, so PackedCostNumericContractTest#hugeJoinProductsSaturateInsteadOfOverflowing and PackedExecutableFallbackTierTest keep their MAX_VALUE expectations; both classes are green in the final module run. Saturated ties are resolved by the 3.8.2 digest, as the critique requested. Minor PackedCostAlgebra NaN: unreachable, because PackedCostVectorArena:97-99 rejects non-finite and negative components at write time. Minor dead UNKNOWN_ROWS_CEILING: no packed ceiling was added. The packed planner's unknown fallback remains statementPatternRows (PIS), and CostVector.UNKNOWN_COMPONENT_ROWS applies only to the CostVector/CascadesPlanner summary path. Minor CostVector.INFINITE: unchanged, so OptimizationGoal.costBound, goalFingerprint and explain output are unaffected. Semantic risk 'pass ratio 0 -> [0,0]': old and new code give the same result, there is no production caller of EstimateVector.filter, and the interval confidence is carried in plannedFilterConfidence.

findings.id: critique reconciliation 3.8.6 (major: exactness only by flag, per-operator empty policy; minors: EvidenceProfile API, wide hypergraph, q-error producers)
findings.rootCause: See the b1 finding 3.8.6: exactness was inferred from confidence 1.0, q-error metrics collapsed uncertainty, semiJoin produced a confident zero, and masks were built as int.
findings.change: Major: exactness comes only from the explicit EvidenceProfile.exact bit. semiJoin with an unproven empty right side keeps the zero point estimate at min(left, right) confidence (documented deviation from the 0.5 floor). An exact empty right side gives an exact empty result. difference() returns `this` for an empty right side (left rows kept), keeps the 0.5 floor for unproven full coverage, and requires exact && right.exact for exactMatchCoverage. BagEstimateMathTest#semiJoinUsesRhsExistenceWhenThereAreNoSharedVariables uses BagEstimate.exact and is green. Minor API: the 10-argument constructor and of(...) are kept as delegating overloads. Minor wide graph: wideFactorHypergraph (PJE:9525) uses PackedNodeSetArena node sets, not int masks. factorHypergraph throws PackedMemoInvariantException above LONG_FACTOR_LIMIT (PJE:11614). Minor q-error producers: traced in b1; no production code writes the five keys onto FactorCostEstimate metrics.
